top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are one sharp invention with a decisive realisation: the magic-wavelength lattice cancels the light shift while many atoms are interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, reaching about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty. The consequences are already measured (clock comparisons, centimetre-level geodesy, bounds on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings), the attribution is compact, and a narrow citation avoids any reliance on redefining the second. P001 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is the broader and also mature achievement and I rank it clearly above no award, but its three-name limit leaves Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan uncredited. No award is the weakest option since both proposals rest on mature, confirmed work.
recusal_note: Possible conflict on P002: my work in atomic physics and laser stabilisation overlaps the clock field, and I spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory, which is close to the frequency-metrology lineage of Ye's group; also Lund and WACQT quantum-sensing ties. No direct tie to Katori or Ye is documented in my profile.
